title: Copilot Studio: agent node runs an AI agent as a workflow step
summary: The briefing's roadmap facts, licensing statements and documented controls are supported. Both API calls are documented, including the allocation request body, and targeted searches found no documentation contradicting the narrowly stated control gaps.

claims.claim: An agent node hands a workflow step to an AI agent that can reason before returning a result.

claims.quote: Equip the agent with tools (Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and connectors) so it can take action.

claims.quote: Knowledge gives the agent something to read. When you ask the agent a question, it can ground its answer in the sources you attach instead of relying only on what the model already knows.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Cost and licensing; Governance controls
claims.claim: Environment allocation and consumption controls apply across Copilot Studio workloads, not only agent nodes.
claims.quote: The capacity and consumption controls in the Power Platform admin center apply across Copilot Studio. They aren't exclusive to the Microsoft Copilot harness. Configure controls with the other Copilot Studio agents, workflows, and features in mind for each environment.

claims.claim: Allocating credits and clearing Draw from the available capacity in my tenant caps prepaid consumption at the environment allocation.
claims.quote: When you clear this option, the environment doesn't draw from unallocated prepaid capacity in the tenant after it consumes its allocation.

claims.claim: Disabling tenant-pool draw does not stop usage through a linked pay-as-you-go billing plan.
claims.quote: This setting doesn't prevent consumption through a pay-as-you-go billing plan linked to the environment.

claims.claim: Azure budgets and alerts notify without stopping Copilot Studio consumption.
claims.quote: Azure budgets and alerts send notifications but don't stop Copilot Studio consumption.

claims.claim: Capacity management requires Power Platform Administrator, Global Administrator or an equivalent role that can manage licensing and capacity.
claims.quote: To manage Copilot Studio capacity, you need the Power Platform Administrator or Global Administrator role, or an equivalent role that can manage licensing and capacity.

claims.claim: The allocation UI is Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Manage Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: In the navigation pane, select Licensing. ... Under Products, select Copilot Studio. ... Select Manage Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: PUT https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=2024-10-01 writes the environment allocation using the supplied body.
claims.quote:
Invoke-RestMethod -Method Put `
    -Uri "$apiBaseUrl/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=$apiVersion" `
    -Headers $headers -ContentType "application/json" -Body $allocationBody

claims.claim: The JSON body supplies scope.environmentId and allocatedEntitlements containing MCSMessages, allocation.quantity and enforcementRules with TenantPool disabled.
The allocation API call requires authenticated authorisation.
claims.quote: $headers = @{ Authorization = "Bearer $($auth.AccessToken)" }

claims.claim: The documented allocation request uses Content-Type: application/json.
claims.quote: -Headers $headers -ContentType "application/json" -Body $allocationBody

claims.quote: When you publish a rule, it governs every environment in the group. The environment-level setting becomes read-only in the Power Platform admin center, and programmatic requests can't override it.

claims.claim: Programmatic requests cannot override the group-governed tenant-draw setting.
claims.quote: The environment-level setting becomes read-only in the Power Platform admin center, and programmatic requests can't override it.

claims.claim: Draw from the available capacity in my tenant is selected by default for eligible Copilot Studio environments without allocation configuration.
claims.quote: For eligible Copilot Studio environments, Draw from the available capacity in my tenant is selected by default when no allocation configuration exists.
